gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Bluetooth doesn't work underwater. A swimmer therefore needs a bone conduction model that stores music on board and plays it in MP3 mode, such as MOJAWA Run Plus, Purra Swim or Shokz OpenSwim Pro. Shokz says its own flagship OpenRun Pro 2 (IP55) 'is not intended for swimming'.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no results, so there were no rival pages to compare against. Its answer recommends bone conduction for 'running or cycling outdoors' and lists 'Noise isolation: Poor'. It never mentions swimming, the IP rating needed for it, the fact that Bluetooth fails underwater, or any codec or multipoint limits on the regular headphones.
decides: This splits the bone conduction pick in two. For running and cycling, OpenRun Pro 2 is fine. For pool or open water, only an IP68 model with built-in storage works, played in MP3 mode: Run Plus at $99.99 or Purra Swim at $169.99. Phone-streamed Bluetooth won't. On the regular-headphone side, Space One's LDAC turns off multipoint, and AeroFit 2's LDAC works only with Android. iPhone owners get AAC on both. This confirms 'regular headphones for sound' but means LDAC is a limited advantage.

findings.label: Swimming exclusion
findings.value: Not for swimming. IP55, 'not designed for submersion'
findings.source_title: OpenRun Pro 2 vs OpenSwim Pro: Which One Should You Choose? (Shokz)
findings.note: Maker's own wording: 'OpenRun Pro 2, however, is not intended for swimming.' and 'OpenRun Pro 2 has an IP55 rating and is not designed for submersion.'

findings.label: Bluetooth underwater
findings.value: Bluetooth signals are disrupted by water, so MP3 mode is required to listen underwater
findings.source_title: OpenRun Pro 2 vs OpenSwim Pro: Which One Should You Choose? (Shokz)
findings.note: Shokz: 'For underwater listening, MP3 Mode is required because Bluetooth signals are disrupted by water.' This is about physics, not one brand, so it applies to every swim headphone, including MOJAWA's.

findings.value: IP68, up to 2 m of fresh water, 32 GB storage, Bluetooth 5.4, $229.95
findings.source_title: OpenRun Pro 2 vs OpenSwim Pro: Which One Should You Choose? (Shokz)
findings.note: Price as listed on the Shokz page. The 2 m depth applies to fresh water 'under specific conditions'.

findings.label: Spare charging cable
findings.value: Type-C Magnetic Charging Cable, $15.90, fits HaptiFit Terra, Run Plus, Purra and Aerra. The Run Air and MOJO2 use a different magnetic cable.

findings.label: LDAC vs multipoint
findings.value: Can't enter multipoint pairing while in LDAC mode. Codecs: SBC, AAC, LDAC. Bluetooth 5.3. 3.5 mm AUX-in turns Bluetooth off. $99.99
findings.note: Maker's wording: 'The headphones cannot enter multipoint connection pairing mode while in LDAC mode.' Battery: 40 h with ANC on, 55 h with it off.

findings.label: LDAC platform limit
findings.value: LDAC 'is only compatible with Android devices'. IP55, Bluetooth 5.4, multipoint yes, 10 h (42 h with case)
findings.note: The page showed $129.99 for the SoloPartner Bundle, not the earbuds alone. IP55, the same rating as OpenRun Pro 2, so it isn't a swim option either.
